items.title: Otters offer hope for Klang River's recovery
items.summary: Small groups of otters are now seen regularly in parts of the city, including along the once heavily polluted Klang River. "Wherever there are otters, there are fish. So that's one of the importance of otters," he said.

items.title: Parents put work aside to support children sitting SPM
items.summary: Faizul Jasman, 46, said he had taken leave to be with his eldest son. "I think our son needs us, at least on the first day. Whenever there's a gap, they hold extra classes, they hold tuition," he said.

items.title: Mother takes SPM to encourage autistic son in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A mother is sitting the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination as a private candidate to encourage her autistic son, who is taking the same examination. Muhammad Adam Daniel Othman, 17, and his mother, Mazlina Abdul Majid, 44, attended the same examination centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Kota Baru for the first day of the written examination, although they were assigned to different examination halls. Mazlina, a dental surgery assistant at the Kota Baru Dental Clinic, said she decided to take the examination to accompany her eldest son, whom she felt was losing motivation.

items.title: RM2.87mil meth haul uncovered in vape cartridges, Chinese tea packets
items.summary: SEPANG: The Customs Department seized methamphetamine worth more than RM2.87 million in two separate operations at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Free Trade Zone on Nov 4 and 14. KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah said the first seizure, on Nov 14, involved 15,456 vape cartridges containing 30.91 litres of liquid suspected to be methamphetamine, worth an estimated RM1.54 million. Initial investigations found that the cartridges had been brought in from Kuching, Sarawak, using Customs declaration forms.

items.title: RM780,000 sought to repair streetlights damaged by cable theft in Putrajaya
items.summary: Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the application was submitted in March this year, but implementation would depend on the ministry's funding priorities. He said the Works Ministry allocated RM840,000 in 2025 under the Peninsular Malaysia Federal Road Maintenance Programme for seven streetlight maintenance projects. Ahmad said road marking works along both directions of FT30, costing RM1 million, were completed on Oct 31.

items.title: Construction, tech stocks lead Bursa losses as Trump's data centre threat rattles investors
items.summary: Real estate investment trusts (REITs) declined 16.89 points, or 1.95 per cent, while healthcare shed 35.05 points, or 2.31 per cent. Utilities fell 31.36 points, or 1.94 per cent, industrial products and services declined 3.37 points, or 2.10 per cent, while energy lost 11.20 points, or 1.51 per cent. Vitrox Corp Bhd fell 39 sen, or 4.47 per cent, to RM8.33, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd lost 36 sen, or 1.82 per cent, to RM19.40.

items.title: 13 Johor water treatment plants at risk amid Super El Nino
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Thirteen water treatment plants (LRA) across five districts in Johor have been identified as at risk of raw water shortages amid projections of a Super El Nino phenomenon lasting until early next year. He said these areas would be prioritised in preparedness measures to ensure uninterrupted water supply to consumers. He said the operations were aimed at boosting rainfall in water catchment areas before dam levels and raw water sources experienced more serious depletion.

items.title: New investment framework to protect local industries from tax breaks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government hopes its new investment incentive framework will prevent tax exemptions granted to foreign companies from undermining local industries, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said. He said the New Incentive Framework (NIF), introduced on March 1, requires investment proposals to undergo a six-part assessment before companies can qualify for incentives. "In 2016, Malaysian companies controlled 85 per cent of the steel industry.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat observes moment of silence for former Dewan Negara deputy president
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat today observed a moment of silence in honour of former Dewan Negara deputy president Datuk Seri Abdul Halim Abd Samad, who died yesterday. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul announced Abdul Halim's death at the start of proceedings and conveyed Parliament's condolences to his family. Abdul Halim, 86, died from a lung infection.

items.title: Grieving father's death, injured SPM candidate determined to sit exams in wheelchair
items.summary: PONTIAN: Despite being offered medical leave and the option of sitting the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations in hospital, Syasya Nasuha Zainal, 17, was determined to attend school today. The eldest of two siblings remained determined to sit the Bahasa Melayu paper, accompanied by her mother, Mirul Fathiah Mustapha, 44. Meanwhile, Mirul Fathiah said she was proud that her eldest daughter remained determined to study and sit the SPM despite losing her father and suffering an injury that left her ankle swollen.

items.title: Malaysia to collect global minimum tax revenue only after June 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will only begin collecting revenue from the global minimum tax (GMT) after June 2027, despite having implemented the tax in January last year. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the collection timeline was determined by financial reporting requirements for multinational companies subject to the 15 per cent minimum effective tax rate. Liew said the GMT was introduced to address profit shifting by multinational companies to jurisdictions offering low or zero corporate tax rates.

items.title: Trump's overseas data centre threat raises fresh risks for Malaysian contractors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: US President Donald Trump's proposed restrictions on American companies building data centres overseas could delay new construction contract awards in Malaysia, raising fresh uncertainty for contractors banking on the country's booming data centre investment pipeline. RHB Research warned that the proposal could trigger another round of uncertainty for Malaysia's construction sector, which has benefited significantly from the influx of data centre investments, particularly in Johor and Selangor. RHB Research said Malaysia's data centre contract awards had previously experienced a slowdown of about four to six months following the announcement of the proposed US AI diffusion rules in January 2025.

items.title: Riding without helmets doubles risk of serious head injuries
items.summary: Peer pressure and a casual attitude towards road safety also contributed to accident risks. The department said parents played a key role in protecting children travelling to school by motorcycle. All road users must obey speed limits, traffic lights and road rules, particularly near schools.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 23, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Monday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street. Market sentiment remains cautious as most prominent would be the highly anticipated Fed rate hike next month. The benchmark index opened 1,547.44.

items.title: 18 schools in Sarawak affected by floods, but SPM unaffected
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN: Eighteen schools in Sarawak have been affected by floods following continuous rain during the northeast monsoon, but all 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination centres remain safe so far. Sarawak Education director Datuk Omar Mahli said the affected schools were in the districts of Subis, Kapit, Kanowit, Miri and Sibu, with no secondary schools affected. Omar said 164 candidates with special needs would also sit the examinations this year, comprising 144 school candidates and the rest private candidates.

items.title: Student sits for SPM despite pain after thigh surgery
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: "I am determined to sit the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination for the sake of my future," said 17-year-old Jeffry Mohammad Noor, who turned up for the written examination today despite still recovering from a road accident. The SPM is Malaysia's national secondary school examination and an important qualification for students seeking to pursue further studies, including matriculation and pre-university programmes. Jeffry, accompanied by his mother, Aliaa Nadiah Abdul Latif, 41, was among 243 candidates from SMK Presint 16 (1) sitting the written SPM examination today.

items.title: 11 Malaysian companies introduce initiatives to strengthen gender equality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: 11 local organisations have introduced 31 workplace initiatives to advance gender equality, improve employee retention and create more inclusive working environments under the country's inaugural Women's Empowerment Principles Corporate Action Lab (WEPsCAL). The initiatives, which have the potential to benefit approximately 23,000 employees, were highlighted at the 2026 Malaysia Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Summit on Nov 17. The programme is part of the UN Women Gender Action Lab, supported by the Australian Government, and delivered through collaboration between the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma), through Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp), UN Women and LeadWomen.

items.title: Iran displays new missile technology, warns US of further 'humiliation'
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States. "A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday. State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards' aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base.

items.title: More wardens for school hostels already in the works, says Education DG
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Education Ministry is working to increase the number of wardens at schools with hostels, with surplus teachers to be deployed to ease the workload of existing wardens. Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the ministry had started appointing assistant wardens through the Malaysia Short-Term Employment Programme (MySTEP) last year and would continue the initiative this year and next. Azam said state and district education departments would coordinate the placement of surplus teachers at schools with hostels to reduce the workload of wardens.

items.title: 304 school students killed in motorcycle crashes since 2024
items.summary: In a statement, the department said 114 students suffered serious injuries and 1,443 sustained minor injuries in 2024. In 2025, 109 students suffered serious injuries and 1,375 sustained minor injuries. Between January and August this year, 49 serious injuries and 898 minor injuries were recorded.

items.title: 19 Kedah schools at risk of flooding during SPM
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Nineteen schools in Kedah have been identified as being at risk of flooding during the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination due to the Northeast Monsoon. Kedah Education Department director Azhari Abdul Rashid said precautionary measures had been taken, including preparing alternative examination centres to ensure candidates were not affected by floods. Azhari said 30,980 candidates had registered for the 2026 SPM examination in Kedah, including 26,148 from government schools.

items.title: Alice Huang reportedly kept contact with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. A spokesman for Jensen Huang declined to comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment.

items.title: More than 51,000 candidates sit for SPM in Johor
items.summary: PONTIAN: A total of 51,371 candidates are sitting for the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination at 367 centres across Johor. Johor education director Zulkurnain Abdul Rahman said 4,484 personnel had been appointed to oversee the examination. At SMK Dato' Penggawa Barat, three examination rooms were operating, with another three quarantine rooms prepared for candidates showing symptoms of fever or infectious diseases.

items.title: 965 SPM candidates in Kelantan face flood risk
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Fourteen Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination centres involving 965 candidates in Kelantan have been identified as being at risk of flooding. She said eight of the centres were in areas where both access routes to examination centres and candidates' homes could be affected by floods. Siti Norina said a total of 27,998 candidates were sitting the 2026 SPM written examinations at 298 centres across Kelantan, which began today.

items.title: SPM candidates in flood-prone areas to be housed in school hostels
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas will be placed at schools with hostel facilities to ensure their examinations are not disrupted. Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the Education Ministry had identified areas frequently affected by floods and sought parents' consent to place candidates in nearby hostels, where meals would be provided free throughout the examination period. "For unexpected situations, we will manage," he said, adding that authorities would help candidates cross flooded roads or arrange alternative transport to examination centres when necessary.

items.title: 18 months after Putra Heights blast, dozens of homes remain unrepaired
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Eighteen months after the Putra Heights gas pipeline explosion, dozens of homes in Taman Putra Harmoni remain damaged, forcing some residents to continue living elsewhere. A check found homes near the blast site still bearing damage to roofs and fences from the intense heat, which reached 1,000 degrees Celsius Many damaged houses remain vacant, with their owners reportedly renting elsewhere or staying with relatives. Residents' representative Loh Poh Heng said the case was proceeding through the courts, with trial scheduled for July next year.

items.title: AI boom drives Malaysia exports to record RM1.81tril, SMEs contribute RM63.6bil
items.summary: E&E shipments jumped 53.9 per cent to RM891.99 billion, reflecting Malaysia's position in global technology supply chains amid rising demand for semiconductors and AI-related infrastructure. Non-E&E exports also recorded strong growth, rising 24 per cent to RM919.17 billion and generating a trade surplus of RM74.03 billion. Among SMEs that participated in Matrade's international trade programmes, 7,434 companies collectively generated RM63.60 billion in exports, supported more than 383,000 jobs and recorded a trade surplus of RM12.04 billion.

items.title: 73,594 Selangor SPM candidates receive food baskets, lunch aid
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A total of 73,594 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates under the Selangor Education Department will receive food assistance and nutritious meals under the 2026 Selangor Nutrition Programme (Nutrisel). He said 71,152 candidates from 256 schools, including national secondary schools (SMK), religious secondary schools (SAM and SAMT), Chinese independent secondary schools (SMPC), special model schools and private tahfiz schools, would receive nutritious lunch sets. Meanwhile, 2,442 candidates from 20 schools and institutions, including boarding schools (SBP), integrated boarding schools (SBPI), national religious secondary schools (SMKA), Selangor Integrated Tahfiz Maahad (MITS), MARA Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) and special education institutions such as Kolej Permata@Pintar, will receive Nutrisel food baskets.

items.title: Translating ICJ's historic judgment into tangible justice for the Rohingya
items.summary: LETTER: Last Thursday, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in its judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar, found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya population in northern Rakhine State during the 2017 military clearance operations. The more difficult question is whether this judicial recognition can be translated into meaningful accountability, reparation and protection for the Rohingya people. By finding that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the Court reinforced a fundamental principle: the prohibition of genocide is not merely a prohibition addressed to individuals.

items.title: HI Mobility bags RM666mil contract for 23 Johor bus routes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Local and cross-border bus operator HI Mobility Bhd has secured an RM665.68 million contract to operate 23 bus routes across Johor Bahru and its surrounding areas for five years under the Stage Bus Service Transformation programme. Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Handal Indah Sdn Bhd, received the letter of acceptance from the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) for the appointment as the intracity bus service network operator. The contract comes amid the broader transformation of Johor Baru's public transport landscape, particularly with the upcoming Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru to Woodlands North in Singapore.

items.title: What new Socso protection and incentives can gig, self-employed workers look forward to in 2027?
items.summary: However, unlike salaried employees, gig workers do not automatically receive the same employment-related social protection. Some measures specifically target e-hailing drivers and p-hailing delivery workers, while others extend to self-employed people in sectors where Socso contributions are not compulsory. What protection does Socso currently offer gig workers and the self-employed?

items.title: Sigh of relief as flood evacuee numbers fall across Selangor and Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Flood situations in Selangor and Perak continued to improve, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres declining to 2,151 people from 615 families this afternoon, compared with 2,315 people from 689 families this morning. In SELANGOR, the number dropped to 1,727 people from 484 families, compared with 1,884 people from 532 families recorded this morning. In PERAK, the number of evacuees at five relief centres in four districts also dropped to 424 people from 131 families this afternoon, compared with 479 people from 157 families this morning.

items.title: ‘There are bound to be waves, but don’t sink the ship’ — Abang Jo tells GPS
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 22 — “Which sea is without rough waters? This was the analogy used by Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg as he reminded the coalition’s component parties to remain united and avoid undermining their consensus ahead of the 13th Sarawak state election. GPS comprises PBB, Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the PDP.

items.title: Stay out of the water, Kelantan beachgoers warned as waves top 1.5-metre
items.summary: TUMPAT, Nov 22 — Red flags have been hoisted at four popular beaches in Kelantan – Pantai Geting, Pantai Cahaya Bulan (PCB), Pantai Irama and Pantai Bisikan Bayu – due to rough sea conditions, with waves exceeding 1.5 metres high. He said the rough sea conditions posed a drowning risk due to high waves and strong currents, including undertows, which could sweep people out to sea even when the water surface appeared calm. Persistent strong northeasterly winds could also result in rough sea conditions and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow rebuts Lim Guan Eng’s RM210m claim, says Penang won’t pay for undelivered water
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 22 — Penang is not required to make any payments to Perak before water supply under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) begins, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said, dismissing claims that the state would have to pay RM210 million annually for 40 years despite receiving no water. He said any payments under the agreement would also be subject to approval by the National Water Services Commission (SPAN). “Therefore, the claim that the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) must pay RM210 million annually for 40 years without receiving a single drop of water is misleading and unethical,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar to host Lao deputy PM as Putrajaya, Vientiane seek closer economic ties
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 22 — Laos Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Thongsavan Phomvihane will undertake a three-day official visit to Malaysia beginning today as both countries mark 60 years of diplomatic relations. In 2025, bilateral trade between Malaysia and Laos increased by 157.8 per cent compared with the previous year, reaching RM258.4 million (US$60.7 million). Malaysia’s exports to Laos amounted to RM77.7 million (US$18.2 million), while imports from Laos totalled RM180.7 million (US$42.6 million).

items.title: Thunderstorm warning issued for parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm today. MetMalaysia said thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in Perlis; parts of Kedah including Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kota Setar and Pokok Sena; and several districts in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Batang Padang, Muallim, Kinta and Kampar. In Selangor, the affected areas are Kuala Langat, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Petaling and Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain to lash parts of Malaysia until 8pm, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: Thunderstorms, heavy rain to lash parts of Malaysia until 8pm, says MetMalaysia PETALING JAYA, Nov 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm today. MetMalaysia said thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in Perlis; parts of Kedah including Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kota Setar and Pokok Sena; and several districts in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Batang Padang, Muallim, Kinta and Kampar. In Selangor, the affected areas are Kuala Langat, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Petaling and Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Stopped, snubbed police, then floored it: Red BMW X6 driver who fled Bukit Bintang roadblock still at large
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — City police are looking for the driver of a red BMW X6 who sped away from a roadblock in Bukit Bintang here at 3.43am last Friday, in an incident that went viral on social media. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah said initial investigations showed the driver stopped at the roadblock on Jalan Bukit Bintang but refused to cooperate with officers before accelerating away. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or visit the nearest police station.

items.title: Bandar Tun Razak gets RM5.7m PM allocation for facility upgrades, Dr Wan Azizah urges residents to help maintain them
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — A total of RM5.7 million in special allocations from the Prime Minister has been channelled to the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency to upgrade various public facilities from 2025 to this year. Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said the facilities upgraded included Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Seri Permaisuri and SK Taman Midah 2 under the MADANI Adopted Schools Programme, aimed at enhancing infrastructure, co-curricular activities and students’ character development, as well as mosques, surau and community halls. We are the residents who use them, so we must look after them together,” she said at the launch of the 2026 MADANI Kita Programme for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency at Perumahan Awam Seri Kota here today, organised by the Federal Territories Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Information Department.

items.title: Half the old rate, please: Kedah consumer group’s plea after BN vows to bring back GST
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — A consumer group today urged the next federal government to consider starting the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at just 3 per cent, half the rate charged before it was scrapped in 2018, should the tax return. Consumers Association of Kedah president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said a lower rate would be more manageable because prices of necessities were already too high compared with people’s incomes. Yusrizal said rising living costs were squeezing consumers and traders alike, as weaker purchasing power slowed business.

items.title: Fadhlina: Values-based education must start in preschool to curb youth social ills
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Values-based education and character building must begin as early as the preschool level to nurture a generation that respects others and demonstrates empathy, says Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said quality education was not merely about teaching children to read, write and count, but also about shaping them into individuals with good values and strong character. Fadhlina also expressed her appreciation for the concern and views expressed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over increasingly worrying social issues involving the young generation.

items.title: ‘Take back Dusun Tua’: DAP gears up to reclaim Selangor seat it handed to Umno in 2023
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 22 — DAP wants Dusun Tua back, with state chairman Ng Sze Han saying the party will contest the seat in the next Selangor election after giving way to Umno in 2023. “In 2018, DAP won in Dusun Tua. However, in the next state election, we will contest and take back Dusun Tua,” the Kinrara assemblyman was quoted as saying.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim unwell, receiving hospital treatment, son confirms
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 22 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is reportedly unwell and is currently receiving treatment at a hospital here. This was confirmed by his son, Naim Ismail, when contacted by Bernama today. “That is correct, (Ismail) is unwell,” he said briefly via WhatsApp.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan swearing-in falls through, source claims some exco nominees pulled out
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 22 — The swearing-in of Negeri Sembilan’s new state executive councillors, reportedly set for Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today, did not take place, Sinar Harian reported. Citing an unnamed source, the Malay newspaper said the ceremony was called off after several people linked to the new line-up allegedly pulled out at the last minute. Local media reported that seven new exco members were expected to form the state administration, down from 10 previously.

items.title: Books, not TikTok: Fahmi calls for early reading habit among children
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Parents should encourage their children to read physical books from an early age to build a strong literacy foundation and prevent them from becoming too absorbed in social media and digital devices, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said without strong reading habits, young people risk spending more time browsing social media platforms such as TikTok rather than exploring quality reading materials that are essential for intellectual development. “Reading books not only builds vocabulary but also provides us with a much broader experience,” he said at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Lembah Pantai MYReaders programme here today.

items.title: Penang survey: State govt scores 70.8pc satisfaction, federal govt 59.6pc
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 22 — The Penang Satisfaction Survey 2026 found that 70.8 per cent of respondents were satisfied with the state government’s performance, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. According to him, Indian respondents recorded the highest satisfaction level with the state government at 82 per cent, followed by Malay respondents at 74 per cent and Chinese respondents at 66 per cent. Chow said the survey found that 59.6 per cent of respondents were satisfied with the federal government, he said.

items.title: Umno open to GE16 talks with Perikatan to ‘ensure that Umno and BN remain relevant’, says VP Khaled
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 22 — Umno cannot expect to win the 16th General Election on its own, vice-president Datuk Seri Khaled Nordin said today as he signalled the party is ready to negotiate with Perikatan Nasional (PN). His remarks come a week after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Barisan Nasional (BN) had no plans to extend its cooperation with PN to the general election. Khaled said a shared political goal should come before differences.

items.title: Anthony Loke: Discuss ‘big tent’ idea in PH Presidential Council, not in the media
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 22 — The “big tent” proposal and other political strategies involving Pakatan Harapan (PH) should first be brought to its Presidential Council for discussion and not aired publicly, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke. Loke also said DAP was open to the proposal for component parties to use their respective party logos in GE16, but this would require further discussions within PH before a final decision was made. On another matter, Loke said the status of his resignation as Transport Minister on Nov 10 was subject to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s decision.

items.title: Zahid’s aide says plan to relocate Rohingya to Turkiye still on, pending clarification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia remains committed to pursuing a proposed relocation of Rohingya refugees to Turkiye under a structured skills training programme, although the initiative remains subject to further clarification and coordination with relevant parties. Shuhaimi Mohamed, press secretary to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said the earlier statement regarding the proposed initiative was issued because efforts were indeed underway, with the ultimate aim of serving the best interests of the country and its people. He said certain matters still required further clarification and coordination with relevant parties before the proposed arrangement could proceed.

items.title: Police foil underground cable theft but suspects flee after chase from Malim Jaya to Alor Gajah
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 22 — Police foiled an attempt by a group of individuals to steal underground cables in Taman Malim Jaya here yesterday, but the suspects managed to escape after a car chase involving several police patrol vehicles. “Checks at the scene found several individuals opening underground utility manhole covers, suspectedly to steal cables, but they fled upon realising the presence of the police. Halim said preliminary investigations found that underground utility manhole covers at Jalan Malim Jaya 2/2 and Malim Jaya Roundabout had been opened, but the individuals had failed to cut the cables.

items.title: Oil blending at sea is banned, but who watches the shore tanks? Maritime Network chief calls for closer monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia’s ambition to strengthen its position as a regional oil trading and bunkering hub requires effective monitoring of petroleum cargoes, including those transferred, stored and handled at shore-based facilities, said Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. Jeyenderan who has raised concerns over the commingling of oil cargoes, said that while international maritime regulations prohibit certain oil-blending activities on board ships during sea voyages, attention must also be given to how petroleum cargoes are handled after they are discharged at ports. In a statement today, he said oil cargoes may be transferred between storage tanks, combined with other products, processed or re-exported before reaching their final destinations.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB appointment up to Yang di-Pertuan Besar, BN won’t interfere, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is leaving the appointment of the next Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar entirely to the discretion of the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he would not act contrary to the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution. Also present were BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.

items.title: BN sitting out Sarawak polls good for state’s stability, says Fadillah as GPS eyes another big win
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 22 — Barisan Nasional’s (BN) decision not to contest in the 13th Sarawak State Election is a positive move towards political stability in the state. Sarawak’s Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) Parliamentary Chief Whip Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said the decision on whether a party should contest an election or otherwise was entirely its prerogative. Besides PBB, GPS comprises Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP).

items.title: Fadillah: 61pc of Malaysians lack RM1,000 in emergency savings, financial literacy must be strengthened
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said this meant that a significant proportion of the population did not have sufficient savings to cope with unexpected circumstances. He said 37 per cent of Malaysians also did not have enough savings to cover three months of expenses in the event of job loss. Therefore, I believe financial literacy is very important and must continue to be enhanced,” he said.

items.title: Flights to Indonesia, Thailand and Brunei: RMAF chief doesn’t rule out meth smuggling abroad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — The drug smuggling ring that has rocked the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) may have reached beyond Malaysia’s borders, its chief has warned. General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the arrested pilots did not fly only between peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, but also on missions to Indonesia, Thailand and Brunei, Berita Harian reported today. Muhamad Norazlan added that the RMAF would not tolerate any misconduct.

items.title: ‘Deal is still on’: Tuition platform keeps its RM200,000 promise to Muar even after Syed Saddiq misses Ironman target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman may have missed his 12-hour Ironman target, but children in Muar will still get the RM200,000 worth of free tuition promised to them. Tuition platform PTTI said in a social media post that it would honour its pledge because the Muar MP had not let it down. After crossing the finish line, the former youth and sports minister apologised to Muar residents for failing to finish within 12 hours, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: BN will reinstate GST ‘immediately’ if it returns to Putrajaya in GE16, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Malaysia could see the return of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) if Barisan Nasional (BN) retakes Putrajaya in the next general election. BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said GST was a fairer and more targeted system than the Sales and Service Tax (SST) now in place, the New Straits Times reported today. According to Zahid, “more than 170 countries have implemented GST, while Malaysia is still implementing SST”.

items.title: Plants growing in toilets that cost 50 sen to use? Johor MB Onn Hafiz loses patience with Larkin Sentral after surprise visit
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 22 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi reprimanded the management of Larkin Sentral over broken facilities, dirty toilets and years of neglected maintenance during a surprise inspection yesterday, Berita Harian reported today. He arrived at 8.30am after complaints and criticism on social media kept growing, and confronted the management over broken seats and lifts, dirty toilets, non-working escalators and potholed roads. Onn Hafiz stressed that basic maintenance should not need repeated intervention.

items.title: Bersatu already talking about life after Muhyiddin, says Azmin Ali
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Bersatu has begun discussing who will lead the party after president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, its secretary-general has confirmed. Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the talks, which include the process of handing over Muhyiddin’s leadership, were being carried out in an orderly manner to keep the party’s struggle going, Berita Harian reported last night. Azmin said Bersatu was being fair to Muhyiddin, who declared three years ago that he no longer wanted to contest in party elections.
